subject.title: Reject unsupported diagnostics OTel grpc config

question: Should OpenClaw stop accepting persisted `diagnostics.otel.protocol: "grpc"` now and rely on doctor to migrate shipped configs, or keep the existing config value until real gRPC exporter support or a longer deprecation path exists?
rationale: The PR fixes a real config/runtime mismatch, but it changes a shipped config enum and doctor may disable enabled telemetry for legacy configs with active OTLP signals, which is a maintainer-owned compatibility decision.

options.title: Accept fail-fast plus doctor migration
options.body: Merge this PR after current-head checks if maintainers agree that clear validation plus repair is the right behavior for unsupported gRPC configs.

options.title: Keep accepting `grpc` for now
options.body: Reject or pause the PR and preserve the current config value until the product has a deprecation window or implements real gRPC export.

options.title: Implement gRPC exporter support
options.body: Use the issue as a feature implementation path instead of narrowing the config contract, with additional dependency and live collector proof.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-fast plus doctor migration
recommendation.body: Merge this PR after current-head checks if maintainers agree that clear validation plus repair is the right behavior for unsupported gRPC configs.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant diagnostics OTel config/runtime surface traces back to their feature commit and recent blamed current-main lines.
